newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse hangs on dollar, interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse hangs on dollar, interest rates.

text.p: The fate of the sinking Brussels bourse hung on the dollar and German interest rates on Monday as investors large and small began unwinding long positions following the sharp decline in New York on Friday.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares .BFX was 2.78 percent, or 67.22 points, lower at 2,350.65 at 0910 GMT having at one stage fallen 3.1 percent. All 20 issues were in the red.
"If the Germans do something on interest rates we could have a problem," one trader said. "They gave an inflation warning last week. First you warn then you act."
The Bundesbank council meets on Thursday.
Traders said the key lay in the strength of the dollar which has been a driving force behind the recent strength of European bourses.
On Monday morning the dollar was below its levels on Thursday -- Friday was a Belgian holiday.
"We have a problem in Europe with the dollar (strength). It is inflationary. The Germans prefer to act quite quickly. They have to maintain their image," a trader said.
Traders said charts indicated support in the Bel-20 at 2,300 points, but moves in the dollar and interest rates could either move the floor down to 2,200 or raise it.
"It is difficult to judge. It could go either way," one trader said. "In Brussels everything depends on the dollar."
Traders said dollar-sensitives and the less liquid stocks were among the main sufferers in the index on Monday.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert was off four percent and chemical firm UCB was down 4.4 percent.
Retailer Delhaize, which has its Food Lion operation in the United States, was 2.9 percent lower.
Outside the index, construction firm CFE was down 12.6 percent, but traders were at a loss to explain why it was under so much pressure.
